messages:
Elena (Finance): @here quick update to p-card and invoice handling that goes into effect next Monday  — small changes but please read. TL;DR: new default monthly card limit is $3,000, teams can request a raised limit (up to $10k) with manager + finance approval, one-off vendor spends > $15,000 require CFO approval, and invoices unpaid > 60 days will be auto-paused until resolved.

Jon (Eng): Curious — does this affect conference registration and hotel bookings if total spend > $3k?

Elena (Finance): Good Q. Yes — travel/ conferences that push a card over the monthly limit need pre-approval. If you expect a big charge, submit a temporary limit increase request in Ramp and tag your manager + finance. For bookings > $2,000 per person, also loop in People Ops if it's employee travel.

Priya (People Ops): Adding: for international travel we still need the usual travel authorization form. Also note per-diem rules unchanged.

Marcus (Sales): What about auto-approved vendor onboarding for recurring SaaS subscriptions under $5k/mo?

Elena (Finance): Subscriptions under $5k/mo remain eligible for delegated approval by Procurement for standard vendors. Anything outside our approved vendor list or with data/security concerns still requires the procurement checklist and legal signoff.

Jon (Eng): Is there a short checklist for one-off vendor spend approvals?

Elena (Finance): Yep — here's the minimal process (paste below). Use the internal approval form and attach SOW/quote + security contact if applicable. We expect approvals within 3 business days normally. If it's urgent, mark as "expedited" and include a justification.

```
Minimal one-off vendor approval checklist:
1) Fill vendor approval form (link in docs)
2) Attach quote or SOW
3) Confirm vendor on approved list OR attach security assessment
4) Manager + Finance approval for <= $15k
5) CFO approval for > $15k
6) Procurement does final onboarding and sets up billing
```

Elena (Finance): Also: starting this cycle we will run a monthly reconciliation sweep. Any transactions with missing receipts older than 14 days will get a reminder from finance-bot; after 30 days we will lock the card until docs are provided.

finance-bot: Reminder: please upload receipts in Ramp within 14 days of transaction to avoid lock. See https://intranet.redwood/finance/pcard for the full policy. :spiral_calendar:

Marcus (Sales): Does the 60-day auto-pause apply to subscriptions too? We occasionally have renewal invoices.

Elena (Finance): Auto-pause applies to any supplier invoices unpaid >60 days. For recurring renewals please set calendar reminders and use Procurement to create a purchase order or committed contract so renewals route through AP automatically.

Jon (Eng): Who do we contact to request the temporary limit bump?

Elena (Finance): Submit a request in Ramp and cc finance@redwood.com. Include expected charge amount, date, and justification. If approved, Finance will post a comment with the approval and the window.

Priya (People Ops): Any changes to expense reimbursements?

Elena (Finance): No change to reimbursement timelines. Expense reports still due within 60 days for reimbursement eligibility. Note: expenses submitted without receipts will be held.

Marcus (Sales): A11y — could we get a tiny one-pager for managers on approving temporary limits? Managers are getting a lot of questions.

Elena (Finance): Good idea — I'll drop a short manager guide by Friday and upload to the intranet. Thanks everyone — ping me or finance@redwood.com with edge cases. :wave:
